evidence: src/application/TaskDtos.ts declares TaskDto, CreateTaskInput and toTaskDto, the module's mapping from domain entities to DTOs.
src/application/CreateTaskUseCase.ts execute(input: CreateTaskInput): TaskDto returns toTaskDto(task).
src/application/MarkTaskDoneUseCase.ts execute(taskId): TaskDto returns toTaskDto(task); src/application/ListProjectTasksUseCase.ts returns TaskDto[] via .map(toTaskDto).
src/application/CreateProjectUseCase.ts execute(name: string): Project returns the domain entity Project directly, with no DTO.
src/application/CreateUserUseCase.ts execute(name: string): User returns the domain entity User directly, with no DTO.
src/application/CreateTaskUseCase.ts and src/application/ListProjectTasksUseCase.ts both contain `if (!this.projects.findById(...)) throw new DomainError("Project does not exist")`.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All six files deal with the same concern: application use cases for a project/task/user tracker. The problem is that the module's outward boundary is inconsistent. The task use cases (CreateTaskUseCase, ListProjectTasksUseCase, MarkTaskDoneUseCase) never return domain entities. They map them to TaskDto through the module's own mapper, toTaskDto, and take input through CreateTaskInput. CreateProjectUseCase and CreateUserUseCase skip this approach and return the domain entities Project and User directly to callers in infrastructure. So half of the module returns DTOs and half returns domain objects, which goes against 'consistent abstraction and boundary'. There is also a smaller duplication: the check that a project exists, with the same DomainError message, is written separately in CreateTaskUseCase and ListProjectTasksUseCase. Neither problem is severe, but together they mean the module fails the 'use the module's abstractions consistently' part of the rubric.

violations.message: execute(name): Project returns a domain entity directly. This skips the DTO boundary that the task use cases set up through TaskDtos.ts (TaskDto/toTaskDto), so the module's output contract is inconsistent.
execute(name): User returns a domain entity directly. This skips the DTO boundary that the other use cases use, so domain objects leak to infrastructure callers in an inconsistent way.
Repeats the project-existence check (`projects.findById` -> DomainError("Project does not exist")) that is also written in CreateTaskUseCase.ts; this rule should live in one place.
